meta.name: golden_aeolus_v2
meta.note: Golden for the claude-fable-5 drafting model (proxy moved off opus-4-8). Middle run of the 3-run variance batch of 2026-08-29 (runs gave 8/16/22 functions; this 16-function run's shape sits closest to golden v1's 18/35/101/92). Accept-all untouched - no engineer edits. granularityBand added 30 Aug with the F1b scorer: 14-24 sub-functions for this SDD (observed 8/16/22 across the batch; 8 was the customer-visible failure mode).

functions.funcDef: Produce and control propulsive thrust for all phases of flight, including the engine-out and asymmetric case.
functions.subDef: Set and regulate thrust on each of four engines in response to thrust-lever and autothrottle commands, with FADEC overspeed/overtemperature protection.

functions.funcDef: Produce and control propulsive thrust for all phases of flight, including the engine-out and asymmetric case.
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust on the ground
functions.subDef: Deploy inboard-engine thrust reversers on the ground, inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement.

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope, including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subName: Control aircraft attitude about three axes
functions.subDef: Command roll, pitch and yaw surfaces in response to pilot and autopilot input via three dissimilar voting flight control computers.

functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope, including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subDef: Position Fowler flaps and leading-edge slats via two independent power drive units on a common torque shaft with per-section asymmetry brakes.

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces and provide braking and directional control on the ground.
functions.subDef: Provide carbon multi-disc braking, normally from system B with system A alternate and accumulator emergency reserve, with per-wheel-pair anti-skid.

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces and provide braking and directional control on the ground.
functions.subDef: Provide hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with a mechanical disconnect for towing.

functions.funcDef: Deploy and stow the landing gear and provide positive lock indication for take-off and landing configuration.
functions.subName: Provide gear extension including alternate means
functions.subDef: Extend the gear by hydraulic system A with a free-fall alternate independent of hydraulic pressure, with independent dual downlock sensing.

functions.funcName: Provide access for loading and secure the payload
functions.funcDef: Open and close the nose visor for straight-in loading and maintain the pressure/lock boundary and payload restraint through all load cases.
functions.subName: Lock and confirm the nose door boundary
functions.subDef: Engage twelve latches and eight independent locking pins, confirm lock via dual dissimilar sensing, and interlock unlock on residual differential below 0.1 psi.

functions.funcName: Provide access for loading and secure the payload
functions.funcDef: Open and close the nose visor for straight-in loading and maintain the pressure/lock boundary and payload restraint through all load cases.
functions.subName: Restrain the payload through all load cases
functions.subDef: Restrain a single blade on nine saddles with two tension straps each and continuously monitor strap tension.

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the pressure differential across the fuselage.
functions.subDef: Regulate differential via two controllers and two outflow valves with pneumatic backup and independent positive/negative relief.

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes across the icing envelope of the certification basis.
functions.subName: Protect airframe surfaces and inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Apply bleed-air protection to wing leading edges and engine cowls and electrical heating to stabiliser zones, probes and windshields.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present flight, navigation and management information and host prioritised crew alerting.
functions.subName: Present flight and navigation information to the crew
functions.subDef: Drive display units and head-up displays from three display processors on dual networks, with an independent standby instrument sharing no supply or sensor.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present flight, navigation and management information and host prioritised crew alerting.
functions.subDef: Consolidate every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures via two independent processing channels.

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them.
functions.subDef: Provide dual-loop continuous detection in engine nacelles and APU, overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays, and smoke detection at nine hold stations.

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them.
functions.subDef: Discharge two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair on crew fire-handle command and an independent APU bottle automatically when unattended.

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for depressurisation, smoke and fume events and the subsequent descent and diversion.
functions.subName: Supply oxygen to crew mask stations
functions.subDef: Feed four quick-donning demand masks from two cross-connected high-pressure cylinders with continuous pressure indication.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to crew command (thrust delivered differs from crew-commanded magnitude), crew aware
fha.effAc: Delivered thrust differs from commanded on one or more engines, producing a thrust error and, if not symmetric across engines, an asymmetry about the 28 m outboard moment arm that the directional-control sizing must counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the anomaly via engine-parameter display and thrust-lever/response mismatch and manages thrust manually / isolates the affected engine (fuel shut-off, fire handle).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded from the function definition alone: the SDD does not bound the magnitude of the erroneous thrust or whether it is symmetric vs asymmetric, and the outcome hinges on crew detectability/arrestability. Need the excursion magnitude, affected-engine count, and crew-response assumption before a §25.1309 class can be derived from effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command, crew aware
fha.effAc: Thrust changes without a crew command; if confined to one side about the 28 m outboard moment arm it produces the asymmetry the directional-control design is sized to counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects via engine-parameter display and manages / isolates the affected engine (fuel shut-off, fire handle).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Not in the model FCIM and unbounded by the SDD: the magnitude, direction (increase vs rollback), affected-engine count and crew-arrestability are not stated, so an aircraft effect cannot be pinned and no severity can be derived. Confirm whether this condition should be authored in the FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response developing below crew detection threshold (crew unaware), crew takes no isolating action
fha.effAc: A thrust error develops without reaching a threshold the crew detects; the crew continue normal duties and take no action, so any asymmetry about the 28 m moment arm persists uncorrected and may grow.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue duties normally and take no action regarding this condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware case removes the crew mitigation, which routinely worsens severity, but the SDD does not state the end-state the undetected error reaches (bounded small error vs. an excursion that develops into an unrecoverable asymmetry). Without that end-effect the severity cannot be derived from effects; classify once the growth/bound is defined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded thrust drift with no crew command, developing below detection threshold
fha.effAc: Thrust drifts slowly without command; if one-sided it introduces a slowly developing asymmetry about the 28 m moment arm that is not annunciated and may go uncorrected.
fha.effCrew: Slow drift may develop below crew detection; if undetected the crew take no action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Not in the model FCIM and unbounded by the SDD: neither the drift rate/final magnitude nor detectability is stated, so the aircraft effect and hence severity cannot be derived. Confirm whether this condition should be authored in the FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of thrust on one side, asymmetric (partial loss of thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Loss of thrust on one side about the 28 m outboard moment arm — the stated directional-control sizing case; aircraft continues to a suitable aerodrome on remaining engines with the rudder authority sized for the outboard-engine-out case, provided the loss is a single engine.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage the asymmetry with rudder and isolate the failed engine (fuel shut-off, fire handle); autothrottle/manual thrust management on remaining engines.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD grounds continued flight to a suitable aerodrome after loss of ONE engine (the design dispatch case), which points below Catastrophic; but loss of a second engine on the same side is explicitly outside the design dispatch case and retained for study, and 'one side' could encompass the two-engine case. Because the number of engines lost drives the class and is not fixed by the condition wording, severity is left empty pending that scope decision (single-engine vs same-side pair).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of thrust generation
fha.effAc: Total loss of thrust from all sources; aircraft cannot maintain level flight and cannot climb or go around. Forced descent leading to inability to reach a suitable landing site in most phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an unpowered forced landing; extreme workload with limited options, most severe at low altitude in take-off/climb.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of thrust generation prevents continued safe flight and landing; forced descent with inability to reach a suitable site. Effects support Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable (1x10^-9/fh). Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight. Reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only and deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock; inadvertent in-flight deployment defeating all inhibits would produce a large asymmetric/drag disturbance. Inboard position at ~0.18 semi-span limits the yawing moment relative to an outboard engine.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to unexpected asymmetry/drag and reverser status; increased workload to counter and to shut down the affected engine.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect of in-flight inadvertent deployment cannot be classified without knowing the aerodynamic/handling consequence of a single inboard-reverser deployment on this configuration, which the SDD does not quantify. The multiple independent inhibits (WOW + radio-altimeter + mechanical lock) bear on likelihood, not on the effect severity. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust not stowing when commanded
fha.effAc: Reverser remains deployed after the crew commands stow during the landing rollout on the two inboard engines. Residual asymmetric drag/thrust and degraded acceleration if a go-around is attempted; effect concentrated on the ground where the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout defines the margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage the deployed reverser during rollout and any go-around decision; workload to control the aircraft and shut down/isolate the affected engine.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a class: the aircraft handling and stopping-distance consequence of a single inboard reverser failing to stow on this configuration is not quantified in the SDD, and the go-around case effect is unknown. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust available on one side only, asymmetric
fha.effAc: On the ground during rollout, reverse thrust available on one inboard engine only, producing asymmetric retarding force and a yawing tendency. On a semi-prepared strip with the stated 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, asymmetric reverse increases directional-control demand and reduces braking-plus-reverse margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter the asymmetry with steering/braking and manage directional control during rollout on a semi-prepared surface; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on whether wheel braking alone (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve) preserves the stopping margin with reverse lost on one side, and on the controllability of the asymmetric yaw on a semi-prepared surface — neither quantified in the SDD. Cannot derive a class; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of reverse thrust on the ground
fha.effAc: Ground deceleration reduced to wheel braking only; landing rollout margin on the semi-prepared strip is eroded (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted); increased overrun exposure if braking is also degraded or the surface is contaminated.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking; increased workload and reduced stopping margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reversers fitted to the inboard pair only and are not the deceleration sizing means; wheel braking is dual-hydraulic with accumulator reserve and carries the ~1,080 m predicted rollout inside the 1,800 m requirement. Loss of reverse thrust erodes the stated margin rather than causing loss of stopping capability — significant reduction in safety margin / increased crew workload. Engineer to confirm against contaminated/degraded-surface landing performance. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches other than as commanded; departure from intended trajectory; potential loss of control if not arrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the mismatch between command and response and attempt to counter; high workload; success depends on remaining pitch authority and phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous response of the aircraft attitude-control function about the pitch axis can produce a loss-of-control departure; even with the crew aware, recovery is not assured in all phases. Engineer to confirm classification and the aware/unaware split against the FCS control-law and reversion architecture. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches with no crew input; unannounced departure from trajectory; potential loss of control before the crew diagnose and counter.
fha.effCrew: No command precedes the motion; crew must first detect the uncommanded excursion, then diagnose and counter; detection and reaction time reduces available recovery margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded pitch motion of the attitude-control function, arriving without a preceding command, can develop into a loss-of-control departure with reduced crew detection and reaction margin. Engineer to confirm against FCS envelope-protection coverage of uncommanded excursions. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls other than as commanded; departure from intended trajectory; potential loss of control if not arrested, aggravated by the large span.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the mismatch between command and response and attempt to counter; high workload; success depends on remaining roll authority and phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous response of the aircraft attitude-control function about the roll axis can produce a loss-of-control departure; even with the crew aware, recovery is not assured in all phases. Engineer to confirm classification and the aware/unaware split against the FCS control-law and reversion architecture. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls with no crew input; unannounced departure from trajectory; potential loss of control before the crew diagnose and counter.
fha.effCrew: No command precedes the motion; crew must first detect the uncommanded excursion, then diagnose and counter; detection and reaction time reduces available recovery margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded roll motion of the attitude-control function, arriving without a preceding command, can develop into a loss-of-control departure with reduced crew detection and reaction margin. Engineer to confirm against FCS envelope-protection coverage of uncommanded excursions. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command
fha.effAc: Attitude control produces yaw different from the crew's rudder/directional command; potential sideslip excursion, at the extreme loss of directional control in the engine-out sizing case (outboard engine at 28 m moment arm).
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the erroneous yaw against expected response and must counter it; increased workload; effectiveness depends on the magnitude and how far the response diverges from command.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous (not covert) yaw is annunciated by the divergence between command and aircraft response, so crew can counter — proposing Hazardous rather than Catastrophic on that basis; ENGINEER TO CONFIRM the transient yaw authority and whether it can reach loss of directional control in the engine-out case, which would drive Catastrophic. Magnitude of erroneous deflection is not bounded by the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no command
fha.effAc: Aircraft yaws with no crew command; sideslip / heading excursion; if sustained, loss of directional control and potential departure from controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: No command reference, so crew must first recognise the uncommanded motion then diagnose and arrest it; recognition delay increases excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded yaw of the primary attitude-control function, occurring without a command reference, can develop into loss of directional control before the crew recognises and counters it — proposing Catastrophic. ENGINEER TO CONFIRM against the achievable uncommanded deflection and reversion authority (split rudder A/B, mechanical reversion to lower segment). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Pitch response diverges from crew command at a rate below the detection threshold; slow attitude / flight-path drift that accumulates toward an envelope excursion (over/under-speed, high load factor, or terrain closure on approach) before it is noticed.
fha.effCrew: By definition the divergence is below the detection threshold, so the crew continue normal duties and take no timely action; recognition occurs late, after significant excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A covert erroneous pitch response of the primary attitude-control function, below the crew detection threshold, removes the crew mitigation and can accumulate to an envelope excursion — proposing Catastrophic. ENGINEER TO CONFIRM the achievable divergence rate and whether monitoring/envelope protection catches it before excursion. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch motion with no command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches slowly with no crew command; flight-path / speed drift toward an envelope limit (over/under-speed, high load factor) that accumulates before recognition.
fha.effCrew: No command reference and slow onset, so the crew continue normal duties until the drift becomes apparent; recognition is delayed relative to the excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A slow uncommanded pitch, without a command reference to alert the crew, can accumulate to an envelope excursion before recognition — proposing Catastrophic. ENGINEER TO CONFIRM the runaway rate (stabiliser/elevator), the available detection/annunciation, and the mechanical reversion authority to the stabiliser trim. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Roll response diverges from crew command below the detection threshold; slow bank / heading drift that accumulates toward a lateral flight-path excursion or unusual attitude before it is noticed.
fha.effCrew: By definition below the detection threshold, so the crew continue normal duties and take no timely action; recognition is late.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft-level effect magnitude: the SDD does not state the achievable erroneous roll authority (two-segment ailerons + multi-function spoilers on hydraulic B/C) or whether a covert roll divergence reaches an unusual-attitude / lateral-excursion outcome versus a counterable degraded condition. Left empty pending the roll transient-authority analysis; do NOT default to a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll motion with no command
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops a slow, unbanked roll divergence not corresponding to any crew or autopilot command; if uncorrected the roll rate builds toward an unusual attitude and loss of lateral control.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive the slow roll on attitude reference and displays and re-establish wings-level manually; workload increases; unusual-attitude recovery may be required if detection is delayed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is bounded by whether/when the crew detect and arrest the divergence. Aware case is likely recoverable (Major-tier), but the rate of divergence and the time-to-detect that would drive the worst-phase (approach/landing) classification are not stated in the function definition. Severity left blank pending divergence-rate and crew-detection assumptions from the PSSA.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response developing below crew detection threshold
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops an erroneous yaw response the crew do not initially detect; sideslip builds and, on this four-engine high-wing configuration with a large outboard moment arm, an undetected yaw/sideslip near the ground or at high speed can progress toward loss of directional control.
fha.effCrew: By definition the crew are below the detection threshold and take no timely corrective action; the divergence continues undetected until it becomes large enough to perceive, by which time recovery margin is reduced.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Directional control is the sizing case for this configuration (outboard engine at 28 m moment arm). An erroneous yaw response the crew cannot detect defeats the crew mitigation and can develop into an unrecoverable directional-control condition in the worst phase; proposed Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh) for engineer confirmation against the directional-control sizing case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded yaw motion with no command
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops a slow uncommanded yaw not corresponding to any command; sideslip and heading drift build and, if uncorrected, progress toward a directional-control divergence, most critical in the takeoff/landing phases on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive the yaw/heading drift and apply rudder to arrest it; workload increases, particularly near the ground; unusual-attitude or directional recovery may be needed if detection is delayed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aware case with a slow onset is likely recoverable, but the worst-phase (takeoff/landing on a semi-prepared surface) outcome depends on the yaw-rate build and time-to-detect, neither of which is stated in the function definition. Severity left blank pending divergence-rate and crew-response assumptions from the PSSA.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Pitch control remains available but at reduced authority; the aircraft can still be controlled about the pitch axis with reduced margin, degraded manoeuvring capability and reduced ability to arrest pitch excursions, most demanding at approach/landing on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain pitch control through the reversion/remaining actuation with increased workload and reduced margin; degraded control law is annunciated; recovery and landing achievable with care.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss (function still performed at reduced capability) of a Catastrophic-tier axis significantly reduces safety margin and increases crew workload, without total loss of the axis — consistent with Hazardous (Severe-Major ↔ Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh). Proposed for engineer confirmation; depends on the amount of authority retained by the mechanical reversion path, which the function definition does not quantify. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Roll control remains available but at reduced authority; the aircraft is still controllable about the roll axis with reduced margin and degraded ability to counter roll disturbances, most demanding at approach/landing and in crosswind on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain roll control at reduced authority with increased workload; degraded law annunciated; landing achievable with care.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss of a Catastrophic-tier control axis reduces safety margin and increases workload without total loss of roll control — consistent with Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh). Proposed for confirmation; the amount of roll authority retained is not quantified in the function definition, so confirm against the FCS actuation/redundancy allocation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of attitude control about all three axes
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be controlled in pitch, roll or yaw; loss of the ability to control trajectory in any phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to command or maintain attitude by any means.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of control about all three axes prevents continued safe flight and landing in every applicable phase; worst case drives Catastrophic. Proposed for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced directional control authority; ability to counter asymmetric-thrust yaw is degraded against the outboard-engine-out sizing case.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains yaw control but with reduced authority/margin, increased workload to hold heading in an asymmetric condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD names outboard engine failure at V1 at the 28 m moment arm as the directional-control sizing case and requires a single rudder-supply loss to still leave sufficient authority; residual authority after this partial loss is not stated in the function definition, so Hazardous is proposed pending the sizing residual — confirm against FCS directional-control sizing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift response to crew selection
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces move to a state other than that selected, giving a configuration inconsistent with the crew's intent during a low-speed phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with a high-lift state not matching selection; corrective action and reconfiguration required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect depends on the magnitude of the erroneous high-lift state (symmetric vs asymmetric, extent) and whether asymmetry brakes limit it; the function definition alone does not state the achievable erroneous configuration or its controllability effect, so severity cannot be grounded.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement with no selection
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces move without a crew selection, changing configuration and lift/drag in whatever phase the movement occurs.
fha.effCrew: Crew faces an unselected configuration change; may require recognition and corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on the flight phase of the uncommanded movement (e.g. clean-configuration cruise vs low speed) and the magnitude/symmetry of movement, neither of which is given by the function definition; severity cannot be grounded.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: High-lift becomes asymmetric across the wing without the crew detecting it, producing an uncommanded rolling/yawing tendency in a low-speed phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the developing asymmetry; continue duties normally, taking no corrective action until effect becomes apparent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The asymmetry brakes at each section are intended to limit asymmetry; the achievable asymmetry that can develop below the detection threshold and its resulting controllability effect are design-dependent and not stated in the function definition, so severity cannot be grounded.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: High-lift control degraded to a single power drive
fha.effAc: High-lift still deployable through the surviving power drive unit via the common torque shaft, at reduced rate/redundancy; the configuration schedule remains achievable but with no further redundancy, so a second-drive failure would become total loss. Performance may require a reduced-flap or alternate-configuration landing with associated speed/distance penalty.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of degraded high-lift; increased workload managing the configuration and applying performance corrections; no immediate loss of control.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated are a significant reduction in functional capability and safety margin plus a meaningful increase in crew workload, with the function still performed — consistent with Major (Remote, 1e-5/fh). PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides
fha.effAc: Asymmetric lift/roll if the asymmetry brakes at each section do not arrest the divergence; the SDD provides asymmetry brakes at each section as the design defence, so the residual aircraft effect depends on brake effectiveness, which is an installation/effectiveness claim not substantiated in the SDD.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the provided material: the aircraft effect turns on whether the per-section asymmetry brakes arrest the divergence before an unrecoverable rolling moment develops. The SDD names the asymmetry brakes but gives no effectiveness/coverage data, so the effect ranges from a contained transient to a roll upset. Missing: asymmetry-brake effectiveness / maximum uncommanded asymmetry.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration control
fha.effAc: No high-lift available: the aircraft is committed to a clean-configuration approach and landing with substantially increased approach and touchdown speeds and landing distance. Against a 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout at MLW, a clean-configuration landing consumes the operating margin and the runway may be inadequate at a semi-prepared strip with no alternate high-lift means.
fha.effCrew: Crew workload markedly increased managing a high-speed clean-configuration approach to a short semi-prepared strip; abnormal procedure and performance recomputation required.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point toward at least Hazardous, but I cannot confirm the class from the material: the outcome depends on whether a clean-configuration landing on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface is survivable/achievable, which requires clean-configuration landing-distance data not in the SDD. Missing: clean-config approach speed and landing distance vs the 1,800 m requirement. Left empty rather than guessing the class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded wheel braking with no crew command
fha.effAc: Inadvertent brake application with no crew command; on take-off roll this degrades acceleration and can compromise the take-off/reject decision, and can cause asymmetric braking with directional deviation and tyre/brake overheat. Anti-skid operates per wheel pair but does not prevent an uncommanded application. On a semi-prepared surface with 20 tyres the directional and stopping-margin effects are aggravated.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an unexpected deceleration/yaw; increased workload and potential reject decision under time pressure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from provided material: the aircraft effect depends on how much brake force can be uncommandedly applied (single wheel/bogie vs multiple), which the SDD does not quantify, and on the take-off-abort consequence. Range spans Major to Hazardous. Missing: worst-case uncommanded braking magnitude and its take-off/directional-control effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to pedal command
fha.effAc: Braking output does not match the commanded pedal input (too much, too little, or asymmetric) during the landing rollout. On the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout, an erroneous/under-braking response erodes the operating margin and risks overrun; an asymmetric response risks directional excursion on an unpaved surface. Alternate braking from system A and accumulator reserve exist but require the fault to be detectable and the correct source selectable.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the erroneous response and revert to alternate/accumulator braking or directional control inputs under time pressure during rollout.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from provided material: the effect depends on the magnitude and symmetry of the braking error and on whether the ~720 m rollout margin absorbs it, none of which is quantified in the SDD. Range spans Major to Hazardous. Missing: worst-case braking error magnitude and resulting stopping-distance/directional effect vs the 1,800 m requirement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of normal wheel braking (system B), alternate braking (system A) available
fha.effAc: Normal braking (system B) lost; alternate braking from system A remains available with anti-skid. Braking capability retained but with reduced redundancy; stopping performance on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip depends on alternate-braking effectiveness against the ~1,080 m predicted rollout margin.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew selects/continues on alternate braking; increased attention to stopping distance and directional control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Alternate braking remains available (dual hydraulic supply to brakes, system A alternate to B per SDD 5.6.2); degraded redundancy with braking retained is a significant increase in crew workload / reduction in safety margin, not a safe-flight-and-landing threat. PROPOSED — confirm against stopping-distance analysis on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface, which the SDD does not contain. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric wheel braking between left and right sides
fha.effAc: Unequal braking force left vs right produces a yawing/steering demand during deceleration; directional control must be maintained by nose-wheel steering and rudder, more demanding on a semi-prepared surface and with the long fuselage. Potential for runway excursion if uncorrected.
fha.effCrew: Crew corrects induced yaw with steering/rudder and modulates braking; increased workload and directional-control demand during a high-workload phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the SDD does not state the magnitude of achievable braking asymmetry, the resulting yaw/steering demand, or the directional-control authority available on a semi-prepared surface. Whether an excursion is credible (Hazardous) or controllable with increased workload (Major) requires a directional-control/excursion analysis not present in the provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection developing below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Anti-skid protection lost without annunciation; crew apply braking normally assuming anti-skid active, so wheel lock, skidding, tyre burst and degraded/asymmetric braking can occur without warning at the moment braking is demanded. Effective stopping distance and directional control degrade against the ~1,080 m / 1,800 m margin with no crew mitigation.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal braking, unaware of the anti-skid loss and take no compensating action; first indication is the skid/lock behaviour itself.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is the crew-unaware split of anti-skid loss: with no annunciation and no compensating action, the outcome is worse than the aware PL2 case and is surface-dependent. Cannot ground the classification (Major vs Hazardous) without the wet/semi-prepared stopping-distance and directional-control margin the SDD does not provide; the absence of annunciation is itself a factor for the engineer to weigh.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking (normal and alternate)
fha.effAc: No system-B or system-A wheel braking. Accumulator-supported emergency braking remains (sized to six full brake applications with all three hydraulic systems lost, SDD 5.4.3/5.6.2/5.6.3); reverse thrust available on the two inboard engines on the ground. With accumulator and reverse thrust exhausted or insufficient, the aircraft cannot be decelerated within the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against the ~1,080 m predicted rollout, with runway-excursion / overrun potential.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew applies emergency (accumulator) braking within its limited application count and deploys reverse thrust on the two inboards; high workload managing a finite braking reserve on a short semi-prepared strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the classification: whether complete loss of wheel braking is Hazardous or Catastrophic depends on whether the accumulator reserve (six applications) plus inboard reverse thrust stop the aircraft within 1,800 m at max landing weight on a semi-prepared surface — a stopping/overrun analysis the SDD does not contain. Left EMPTY rather than assumed. PROPOSED effects stated; severity to be derived from that analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground directional steering control
fha.effAc: No directional steering input available on the ground; directional control on the ground reverts to differential braking and (where available) rudder/thrust, with reduced authority. On a semi-prepared 1,800 m strip against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout the reduced margin for lateral control is a sizing-sensitive factor.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware (annunciated); must maintain directional control by differential braking/rudder, increased workload during high-speed roll and taxi.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is aware and ground-phase only; outcome depends on whether differential braking/rudder retains adequate lateral control on the semi-prepared surface within the 1,800 m / ~1,080 m margin. The SDD states the requirement and predicted rollout but does not establish the controllability outcome of steering loss on that surface; classification requires directional-control/controllability engineering judgement not supplied. Left empty pending that assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced ground steering authority / range
fha.effAc: Steering available but at reduced authority or range; degraded ground manoeuvring, may require larger radii and greater use of differential braking to hold centreline on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware (annunciated/degraded feel); increased workload, may require reduced taxi speed and greater anticipation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aware, ground-phase, partial degradation. Whether reduced authority still permits safe directional control within the strip lateral margin is not established by the SDD; classification requires controllability judgement on the residual authority, not supplied. Left empty rather than defaulted.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous steering response to crew command
fha.effAc: Nose wheel deflects in a direction/magnitude different from commanded; aircraft departs intended ground track. At take-off/landing-roll speed an erroneous deflection can cause a rapid lateral excursion toward the edge of the strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of unexpected track deviation; must recognise and counter by opposite command / differential braking, with limited time margin at speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Erroneous ground steering at speed is a directional-control excursion whose severity depends on how quickly the crew can detect and counter it and on the lateral margin available on the semi-prepared strip. The SDD does not establish the excursion dynamics or recoverability; classification requires ground-controllability judgement not supplied. Left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded steering deflection with no command
fha.effAc: Nose wheel deflects with no crew command; aircraft yaws off intended track. At take-off/landing-roll speed an uncommanded deflection drives a lateral excursion toward the strip edge.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of unexpected track deviation; must recognise the uncommanded input and counter by differential braking/rudder, limited time margin at speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Uncommanded ground steering deflection at speed is a directional-control excursion; severity depends on detection/recovery time and lateral margin on the semi-prepared strip, neither established by the SDD. Classification requires ground-controllability judgement not supplied. Left empty. Note: this condition is not currently in the SF-006 FCIM (which carries M and M3) — reconcile whether M2 is distinct.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded steering deflection developing below crew detection while not active
fha.effAc: A steering deflection develops below the threshold at which the crew detect it while steering is not actively being commanded; the aircraft track drifts progressively off centreline before the crew react.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware initially; continue normal duties and take no corrective action until the deviation grows large enough to detect, reducing the margin to counter it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware, below-detection development removes early crew correction; severity depends on the growth rate of the deflection, the detection threshold, and the lateral margin on the semi-prepared strip. None of these are established by the SDD; classification requires ground-controllability and detectability judgement not supplied. Left empty rather than defaulted.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of gear extension by all means (normal and free-fall alternate)
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot achieve a normal gear-down configuration by any means; a gear-up or partial landing results with airframe damage on touchdown.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via gear position indication and unsafe-gear alerting; execute abnormal/emergency landing procedures with degraded outcome.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a severe outcome but the FHA cannot fix the class without the substantiated survivability of a gear-up landing on the semi-prepared strip and the assessed injury/hull outcome; leaving severity blank pending that engineering input rather than reaching for Catastrophic or Hazardous.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of normal (hydraulic system A) extension, free-fall alternate means available
fha.effAc: Normal extension unavailable; gear extended by free-fall alternate, independent of hydraulic pressure; normal landing achievable.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware; select alternate free-fall extension from a separate handle and confirm downlocks; increased workload, procedure available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With a successful independent alternate extension the aircraft effect is a workload/procedure event; classification (Minor vs No Safety Effect) needs the crew workload assessment and confirmation the alternate reliably achieves down-and-locked — not grounded here, so left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric or incomplete extension (crew aware)
fha.effAc: One or more gear units not down-and-locked; aircraft touches down in an asymmetric/partial gear configuration with airframe damage and possible directional excursion on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via gear position and downlock indication; attempt recycling/alternate extension and prepare for abnormal landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Asymmetric/partial touchdown effect could support Hazardous or worse, but the class depends on assessed controllability and damage on a semi-prepared surface at landing weight, which is not established in the inputs; left blank rather than presumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: False downlock confirmation with gear not locked, both sensing circuits agreeing (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Gear indicated down-and-locked but not locked; on touchdown a leg collapses, producing airframe damage and a directional excursion on the semi-prepared strip with no prior crew action.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware — both independent proximity circuits agree on a false locked state; crew continue a normal landing and take no corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected false-locked leading to a gear collapse at touchdown is a plausibly severe (potentially Hazardous/Catastrophic) misleading-indication condition, but the class depends on the assessed touchdown outcome/controllability and injury/hull result — not established in the inputs; left blank rather than assumed. Note the common-mode agreement of two dissimilar-routed circuits is itself an independence claim to be tested.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose boundary lock and confirmation
fha.effAc: Nose visor is the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed; complete loss of lock and confirmation means no assured means to hold or verify the boundary. In flight this risks loss of the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path.
fha.effCrew: No valid lock indication available to the crew; take-off configuration check cannot be satisfied from this function.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unlocked/uncontained pressure-boundary and primary structural load-path door in flight leads to loss of the aircraft; classified Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10^-9/fh) for engineer confirmation. Door is ground-operated only (§5.7.6), so the exposure is a latch/lock failing to hold, not an in-flight unlock. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Boundary unlocked with no unlock command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded unlock of a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage structural load-path door; in flight risks loss of the pressure boundary and structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Lock status changes without crew command; crew reacts to indication where available.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded unlock of a door that is the pressure boundary and primary structural load path in flight leads to loss of the aircraft; Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10^-9/fh) proposed for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: False locked confirmation with boundary not fully secured, both sensing paths agreeing
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar sensing paths falsely confirm locked while the boundary is not fully secured; the take-off configuration monitor is defeated, permitting operation with the pressure boundary and structural load path not secured, which can progress to loss of the boundary in flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives valid-appearing locked indication and configuration confirmation; no cue that the boundary is unsecured.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false-locked confirmation on both dissimilar sensing paths defeats the take-off configuration check (§5.7.4) and can permit dispatch with the boundary unsecured, leading to loss of the aircraft in flight; Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1×10^-9/fh) proposed for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one independent lock-confirmation path
fha.effAc: One of the two dissimilar, independently routed lock-confirmation paths is lost; the second dissimilar path plus the physical latches and pins remain. The SDD does not state an aircraft-level effect for single-path loss.
fha.effCrew: One confirmation means remains available to the crew for the take-off configuration check.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an adverse aircraft-level effect from the function/FCIM alone: the second dissimilar sensing path and the physical latches/pins remain (§5.7.2). Whether single-path loss is No Safety Effect or Minor depends on dispatch/MEL treatment not stated in the SDD — severity left empty pending that input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous strap tension (over- or under-tension) at a single restraint station
fha.effAc: Over- or under-tension at one station; blade retained by remaining straps and saddle geometry per sized single-strap-loss margin; potential local load-path exceedance at the affected saddle/hard point.
fha.effCrew: Condition annunciated by the tension monitoring loop; crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Proposed Major on the basis that the SDD sizes load paths so loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, bounding a single-station tension error; left EMPTY pending confirmation because whether over-tension exceeds a saddle/hard-point structural limit (no redundancy in hard points) is a loads/structures determination not resolvable from the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint-status indication from the single tension-monitoring loop
fha.effCrew: Restraint status is a single instrumented loop; erroneous indication is misleading and may mask an actual restraint loss or present a false alarm; crew has indication only with no in-flight adjustment.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD provides indication-only in flight with no in-flight restraint adjustment, so the aircraft-level consequence of the crew acting or not acting on erroneous status is not determinable from the document; the effect depends on the underlying true restraint state and on procedural response not specified here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint at two adjacent stations
fha.effAc: Loss at two adjacent stations exceeds the sized single-strap-loss case; potential longitudinal migration of the 72.6 t unitised blade with attendant centre-of-gravity shift and load-path challenge.
fha.effCrew: Annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention; crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Proposed Hazardous: two-adjacent-station loss is the SDD's declared 'restraint condition requiring immediate attention' and exceeds the sized single-strap-loss margin, creating potential CG/loads effect on a 72.6 t mass; left EMPTY pending confirmation because the magnitude of any resulting CG excursion / controllability effect is a loads and flight-controls determination not stated in the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint developing without annunciation on the single tension-monitoring loop (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Progressive restraint loss with no annunciation from the single monitoring loop; crew continue normal duties and take no action; potential uncontrolled longitudinal migration of the 72.6 t unitised blade with major centre-of-gravity excursion challenging continued controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware — the single tension-monitoring loop provides no annunciation; no in-flight adjustment available; crew continue their duties normally.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Proposed Catastrophic: an unannunciated, progressive loss of restraint on a single monitoring loop leaves the crew unaware of an uncontrolled 72.6 t mass migration and potential large CG excursion, which for the unaware case can challenge continued controlled flight; left EMPTY pending confirmation because the CG-excursion-to-controllability consequence is a loads/flight-controls substantiation not provided in the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint through all load cases
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Unrestrained single unitised blade (up to 72.6 t, up to 105 m) free to translate/shift along the hold axis; large uncommanded CG excursion beyond limits and potential overload of hold floor hard points and airframe; loss of controllability and structural integrity credible.
fha.effCrew: Sudden severe CG shift and pitch upset; control demands potentially beyond available authority; task load overwhelming with no in-flight means to re-restrain.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed in the hold.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from the design payload: a single 72.6 t blade carried whole along the hold axis with no in-flight restraint adjustment and no redundancy in hold floor hard points; total loss of restraint through load cases permits a mass shift capable of CG excursion beyond limits and structural/controllability loss — effects support Catastrophic. Confirm against the actual restraint load-case analysis. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fuselage differential pressure control
fha.effAc: No active control of fuselage differential; hold and flight-deck pressurisation uncontrolled. Independent mechanical positive/negative relief valves still protect the structure from over/under-pressure limits.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information display

fha.fcDesc: Loss of overheat detection in a monitored run
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Overheat detection is lost on a monitored run (bleed duct run or main gear bay); a developing overheat on that run would not be annunciated, so the crew cannot act on it (e.g. isolate a leaking bleed duct or manage a hot gear bay).
fha.effCrew: No overheat warning for the affected run; crew continue normal duties and take no isolating action against an overheat there.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect (loss of overheat monitoring on one run) is grounded, but the class depends on the consequence of an undetected bleed-duct or gear-bay overheat (duct rupture, hot-air damage, tyre/brake overheat) and on any independent indication — not derivable from the function definition alone. Left blank; confirm the worst-phase consequence of an undetected overheat on the affected run.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of hold smoke detection
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Hold smoke detection (nine stations along the hold length) is lost; a fire/smoke event in the hold would not be annunciated. The hold has no suppression fitted and carries a single non-combustible blade with no combustible palletised load; crew have no in-flight suppression means regardless of detection.
fha.effCrew: No smoke warning for the hold; crew continue normal duties and take no action against a hold event they cannot detect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect (loss of hold smoke detection) is grounded, but the class depends on the substantiation of the recorded 'detection but no suppression' decision and the fire risk of a hold carrying only a single non-combustible blade — an assumption the SDD itself flags as to be substantiated. Cannot classify from the function definition; left blank pending that substantiation and the worst-phase hold-fire consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of a detection loop within a zone
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One of the two detection loops within a zone is lost undetected; detection continues on single-loop logic (dual-loop AND for warning degrades to single-loop on loss of one loop), so fire/overheat warning for that zone remains available but on a single, now non-redundant, path with the loss latent.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of the latent loop loss; crew retain fire/overheat warning for the zone via the surviving loop and continue normal duties.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Detection remains available on the surviving loop per the SDD's single-loop degradation, so this is a latent reduction in detection redundancy rather than a loss of warning. Its class depends on the exposure-time / combination with a subsequent second-loop loss or coincident fire — a latency/independence judgement not settled by the function definition. Left blank rather than assume a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in any protected zone (engine nacelles 1-4, APU compartment, bleed ducts, main gear bays, hold smoke detection). An undetected engine/APU fire can progress uncontained; the crew cannot initiate extinguishing because no warning is presented, defeating the fire-handle response.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of a developing fire; no fire warning, no procedure trigger; loss of the primary means to command extinguishing at the right time.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected fire in an engine or APU fire zone that progresses without any warning or crew response can lead to structural/system loss; total loss of detection across all fire zones removes the safeguard against an uncontained fire. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge
fha.effAc: Extinguishing agent discharged into a protected zone with no fire present, expending an engine-pair bottle; that zone's remaining charge is reduced or exhausted, degrading fire-suppression availability for a subsequent real event in the same engine pair.
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with discharge status; must manage a false discharge and account for reduced extinguishing capability for the remainder of the flight.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is expended agent / reduced suppression availability rather than an immediate hazard; whether this is Minor or Major depends on remaining bottle coverage after a single inadvertent discharge and the exposure to a subsequent real fire in the affected engine pair — not established by the SDD. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Extinguishant discharge into the wrong zone
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect: the SDD establishes cross-plumbing only WITHIN an engine pair (either bottle to either nacelle of the pair) and dedicated APU protection; it does not define a mis-routing path to a genuinely wrong zone, nor the effect of agent delivered where no fire exists while the real zone goes unsuppressed. Aircraft/crew effects and severity left empty pending architecture confirmation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing in one protected zone
fha.effAc: No extinguishing capability available in one protected zone; a fire in that zone (an engine nacelle or the APU compartment) cannot be extinguished and may progress uncontained. Detection remains, so the fire is annunciated, but the means to suppress it is absent for that zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives the fire warning but the fire-handle command produces no extinguishing effect in the affected zone; no means to control the fire in that zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontrollable fire in a single engine or APU fire zone, with detection present but no suppression, is a severe condition; loss limited to one zone (other zones retain cross-plumbed/independent protection) supports Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. Proposed for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one extinguisher agent charge
fha.effAc: One extinguisher bottle unavailable within an engine pair; the pair retains its second cross-plumbed bottle, so a first-shot discharge into either nacelle of the pair remains available. Suppression margin is reduced (single shot rather than two) for that pair.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains a fire-extinguishing means for the affected engine pair via the remaining cross-plumbed bottle; reduced reserve against a re-flash or a second event.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With cross-plumbing, one lost charge still leaves a functional shot for either nacelle of the pair, so the immediate effect is reduced reserve rather than loss of capability; classifying Minor vs Major requires the exposure to a second/re-flash event and dispatch assumptions not stated in the SDD. Left empty pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected unavailability of an extinguisher charge (one bottle of a cross-plumbed pair, crew unaware)
fha.effAc: One extinguisher charge unavailable; per SDD each engine pair is served by two cross-plumbed bottles, so a single fire discharge remains possible; margin against a two-shot need is silently reduced
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of degraded suppression reserve; would attempt normal discharge on a fire event, unaware a shot may be missing
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive: SDD confirms two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair so first-shot capability persists, but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of an undetected single-charge loss coincident with a fire requiring a second shot. Missing: whether one shot is sufficient for the sizing fire case, and exposure of the undetected condition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing capability in all protected zones
fha.effAc: No means to extinguish an engine-nacelle or APU-compartment fire; an in-flight fire in a high-energy, flammable-fluid zone would progress unchecked, threatening the engine, pylon, wing structure and fuel
fha.effCrew: Fire detection remains but fire handles cannot extinguish; crew limited to shutdown/fuel-isolation and expedited diversion
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh): an uncontrolled fire in a nacelle/APU zone described as high-energy, flammable-fluid can propagate to wing fuel and primary structure; total loss of extinguishing removes the only suppression means. Engineer to confirm against the credible fire progression and detection-only mitigation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous free-flow / overpressure discharge of crew oxygen supply
fha.effAc: Uncommanded free-flow depletes the gaseous cylinders; overpressure vents overboard via the thermal discharge indicator; no oxygen available for a subsequent depressurisation or smoke/fume event
fha.effCrew: Loss of protective breathing reserve; on a later cabin-altitude or smoke event the crew would be without oxygen for the diversion; possible in-cabin oxygen enrichment increasing fire risk
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive without a coincident-event assumption: consequence depends on whether a depressurisation/smoke event follows the depletion and on the max-operating-altitude (FL260) time-of-useful-consciousness. Missing: whether erroneous free-flow alone is annunciated and rechargeable, and the combined-condition exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous oxygen system status or pressure indication presented to the crew
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; oxygen delivery capability is unchanged
fha.effCrew: Misleading cylinder-pressure/status indication; crew may dispatch or continue believing reserve adequate when it is not, or divert unnecessarily on a false low indication; cylinder pressure is a dispatch item
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive: effect depends on the true underlying oxygen state the erroneous indication masks and on crew reliance during a subsequent depressurisation. SDD states pressure is a dispatch item and displayed continuously but does not state the aircraft-level outcome when the indication is wrong.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen supply at one or more mask stations
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect on trajectory; reduced or lost crew protective-breathing capability at affected station(s)
fha.effCrew: Affected crew member(s) without oxygen during a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; independent per-mask regulators and a two-cylinder crossover mean a single failure may leave other stations supplied, but loss at a piloting station during a cabin-altitude event risks incapacitation
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive without operational assumptions: consequence depends on which/how many stations, coincidence with a depressurisation or smoke event, and FL260 time-of-useful-consciousness. SDD gives per-mask independent regulators and a crossover but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of station loss.. Engineer to classify.

assumptions.text: The hold carries only a single non-combustible blade with no combustible palletised load, so the fire risk of losing hold smoke detection is bounded by that payload assumption.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the no-suppression decision as an assumption to be substantiated and bases it on the single non-combustible blade payload.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a combustible payload case exists or the no-suppression decision is not substantiated, SF-014-PL3 severity is driven upward.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-014-PL3 effect statement and blank severity

citations.quote: the hold carries a single blade and no combustible palletised load, and hold suppression is deliberately not fitted

assumptions.text: Total loss of fire/overheat detection means an engine or APU fire can develop and progress with no crew warning and no extinguishing response.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA must state an aircraft effect for SF-014-TL, but the SDD describes only the detection architecture, not the outcome of a completely undetected fire.
assumptions.ifWrong: If some independent/alternative detection or an inherently fire-tolerant zone limits the consequence of undetected fire, SF-014-TL could reduce below Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Each engine nacelle and the APU compartment carry dual-loop continuous fire detection

assumptions.text: Loss of extinguishing in a single zone leaves an uncontrollable fire in that engine/APU zone while other zones retain protection.
assumptions.rationale: Needed to place SF-015-PL on the severity ladder; the SDD gives per-pair cross-plumbing and independent APU protection but not the aircraft-level consequence of one zone losing suppression.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single-zone suppression loss is bounded by a benign zone (e.g. limited fire load) or an alternative means, SF-015-PL could reduce from Hazardous.

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair

assumptions.text: SF-015-PL2 (loss of one extinguisher agent charge) is a project failure condition even though the model's SF-015 FCIM lists PL and PL3, not PL2.
assumptions.rationale: The turn instruction names SF-015-PL2, but no such condition id appears in the SF-015 rows of CURRENT PROJECT STATE.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-015-PL2 does not exist in the model, this row should be deleted or its srcCondId corrected before it is accepted.

assumptions.text: The flight crew, not passengers, are the only occupants and the hold is unoccupied in flight for every occupant-effect assessment.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant-effect column requires knowing who is aboard; the provided model has no passenger data so the SDD statement governs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, the occupant effects and hence severities for oxygen and fire conditions would escalate.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-015-TL, SF-015-PL3, SF-016-M, SF-016-M2, SF-016-PL

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: An engine-nacelle or APU fire, if not extinguished, can credibly propagate to wing fuel and primary structure given the nacelle zone environment.
assumptions.rationale: Deriving the SF-015-TL severity requires a credible fire-progression outcome; the SDD characterises the zone but does not state the end effect.
assumptions.ifWrong: If fire cannot propagate beyond a self-limiting nacelle, SF-015-TL could drop below Catastrophic.

citations.quote: High energy, flammable fluid, fire zone

assumptions.text: The severity of complete loss of crew oxygen (SF-016-TL) is driven by coincidence with a smoke/fume or depressurisation event, not by loss of oxygen in un-eventful pressurised flight.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states what the oxygen system is FOR but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of losing it, nor whether the credited threat is coincident or independent; the classification hinges on this.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of oxygen alone (no coincident event) is the credited condition, SF-016-TL is not Catastrophic — it becomes a dispatch/continuation matter and the severity drops, likely to Major or below.

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and for the descent and diversion that follow

assumptions.text: The low hold differential and FL260 maximum operating altitude make an un-protected depressurisation less time-critical than on a high-altitude transport, but the flight-deck cabin altitude is conventional and still requires oxygen protection.
assumptions.rationale: The document gives FL260 ceiling, a low HOLD differential, and a conventional flight-deck cabin altitude, but does not state the resulting time-of-useful-consciousness or the protected descent profile that sets severity.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the flight-deck cabin altitude at FL260 is benign enough to not require oxygen for a survivable descent, SF-016-TL and SF-016-PL2 severities reduce.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016-TL and SF-016-PL2 effCrew and severity

citations.quote: The flight deck is held at a conventional cabin altitude; the hold is pressurised to a low differential only

assumptions.text: The oxygen system is the sole means of crew breathing-oxygen protection (no alternative source).
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes only the two-cylinder gaseous system with no other crew-oxygen provision; needed to treat TL as total loss of capability.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an alternative crew-oxygen source exists, SF-016-TL is not a complete loss of the capability and severity reduces.
